scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

problem_definition_history.requested_solution: SH-CS (the requester) asked for an AI agent to auto-answer billing dispute tickets and automatically fix whatever is causing the wrong bills (CL-01).
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume rose from ~600/month in Jun-Jul 2026 to ~1180-1260/month in Aug-Sep 2026, a ~2x increase (E-07).
59% of disputed bills were billed from ACTUAL reads vs 41% from ESTIMATED reads (E-01), i.e. most disputes are not tied to estimate substitution.
Manual-read route completion fell to 0.88 against a 0.95 target across 9200 accounts in Aug-Sep 2026 (E-05).
CS dispute response times remain within the 3.0-day SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d, E-03), so response speed is not degraded.
problem_definition_history.root_problem: Since August 2026, billing dispute tickets have roughly doubled (E-07), driven by a billing-side defect in the billing import/validation step that produces incorrect bills predominantly from ACTUAL (non-estimated) meter reads rather than from estimate substitution (E-01: 59% ACTUAL vs 41% ESTIMATED among disputed bills), with tariff/rate changes ruled out as the mechanism (E-02, E-04).

challenges.rationale: ER-1: premise E-01 revised by E-11: Still shows the raw count split: 1240/3025 (41%) disputed bills were ESTIMATED, 1785/3025 (59%) were ACTUAL. It no longer supports a uniform billing-side defect hitting both read types: E-11 shows the ESTIMATED cohort's dominant mechanism is a specific AMI-read import rejection, distinct from any (still unconfirmed) ACTUAL-read mechanism, so the ACTUAL-vs-ESTIMATED split cannot be read as evidence of one common defect.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

H-CS-RESPONSE-FRAMING.statement: The dispute surge is primarily a Customer Service response-capacity problem, and an auto-answering/auto-fixing AI agent would resolve it as requested.

H-FIELD-HANDOFF-FAILURE.statement: The manual meter-read handoff from Field Services to Billing degraded (delivery or semantic validity), increasing estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTFALL.statement: Field reading staffing/route completion shortfalls caused missed manual reads, forcing estimates and driving disputes, as SH-FIELD's own framing suggests.

U-IMPORT-RULE-CHANGE-ROOT-CAUS.question: Did a billing import validation rule change (DA-RULES/billing-config) occur around August 2026, and does its scope match the pattern of errors seen on ACTUAL-read bills?
U-IMPORT-RULE-CHANGE-ROOT-CAUS.decision_impact: Determines whether the specific import-rule defect can be confirmed and documented as required by SC-DEFECT-LOCATED; without it the root mechanism remains a candidate, not an established cause.
U-IMPORT-RULE-CHANGE-ROOT-CAUS.resolution_path: Query the billing-config rule-change log (DA-RULES) for changes around August 2026 and compare the affected record pattern to ACTUAL-read disputed bills in DA-BILL.
U-IMPORT-RULE-CHANGE-ROOT-CAUS.safe_placeholder: Continue diagnostic analysis on DA-BILL/DA-TICKET; withhold any claim that the defect is located until the rule-change pattern is confirmed.

U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.question: Does the degraded mdms-export tool / pending vendor access (recovery_decision HOLD, ACCESS_PENDING) hide a contributing AMI read-validity issue affecting the ESTIMATED-read minority of disputes?
U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.decision_impact: If an AMI read-validity issue exists, the ESTIMATED-read minority of disputes may have a separate vendor-side contributing cause requiring a different remediation path from the ACTUAL-read defect.
U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.resolution_path: Await Telemetrix vendor provisioning of mdms-export access (currently HOLD/ACCESS_PENDING) and pull read_events_for_disputed_estimated once available.
U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.safe_placeholder: Proceed with ACTUAL-read defect diagnosis independent of MDMS access; flag ESTIMATED-read minority analysis as pending vendor access.
U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.resolution: The mdms-export query (E-11) is authoritative and complete, confirming a real AMI read-validity/import issue (high-consumption rejection) affecting 1184 of the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills, directly answering that AMI-side processing does contribute to the ESTIMATED-read dispute minority.

U-BASELINE-READ-TYPE-DISTRIBUT.question: What is the ACTUAL/ESTIMATED read-type split among the overall (non-disputed) bill population for Aug-Sep 2026, to confirm the 59%/41% disputed-bill split (E-01) is anomalous rather than the normal billing mix?
U-BASELINE-READ-TYPE-DISTRIBUT.decision_impact: Confirms whether the ACTUAL-read skew in disputes (E-01) is itself evidence of a defect or simply reflects the normal billing population mix, affecting how SC-DEFECT-LOCATED is validated.
U-BASELINE-READ-TYPE-DISTRIBUT.resolution_path: Pull the overall (non-disputed) bill population read-type split from billing-db for Aug-Sep 2026 and compare it to E-01's disputed-bill split.
U-BASELINE-READ-TYPE-DISTRIBUT.safe_placeholder: Treat the 59% ACTUAL figure as provisional evidence of anomaly pending baseline comparison; do not finalize defect location solely on disputed-bill mix.

A-DISPUTED-MIX-REPRESENTATIVE.statement: The 59%/41% ACTUAL/ESTIMATED split among disputed bills (E-01) reflects where a billing-side defect concentrates, not merely the baseline mix of all bills issued, since the overall-population distribution has not been measured.

A-DEFECT-TIMING-AUGUST.statement: The billing-side defect producing wrong ACTUAL-read bills began around August 2026, coinciding with the dispute surge, even though billing-config rule-change evidence has not yet been pulled to confirm timing.

A-FIELD-SHORTFALL-SECONDARY.statement: The field route-completion shortfall (E-05) and claimed staffing gap (E-06) are a real but secondary contributor affecting only the ESTIMATED-read minority of disputes, not the primary driver of the overall surge.
